chunks: From him, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two, who said:
There is no option (for the wife to choose divorce) except during a period of purity from which intercourse has been avoided, in the presence of witnesses.

key_terms.خِيَار: Option/choice (specifically the wife's right to choose divorce)
key_terms.طُهْر: Purity (referring to the period between menstrual cycles)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific conditions for a wife to exercise the right of choosing divorce in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-istibsar establishes the strict temporal condition for a valid 'option of divorce' (ikhtiyar) by the wife, requiring the period of purity (tuhr) to be free from sexual intercourse (jam') to ensure clear lineage. The requirement of witnesses (shuhud) underscores the public and formal nature of this irrevocable or revocable act within Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing it from informal separations. This ruling is pivotal in understanding the procedural safeguards against paternity disputes in early Shia legal theory.
